# Big O Mathematics

#### Course: Complexity Calculation

## Big O Mathematics

Now, let's return to the mathematical interpretation of Big O.

Example

Given the following function,

```python
f(n) = 4n + 3
```

Our goal is to find a function c * g(n) such that the following conditions are satisfied:

```text
f(n)≤c∗g(n)f(n) \leq c*g(n)f(n)≤c∗g(n)n≥n0n \geq n_0n≥n0​c>0c > 0c>0n0≥1n_0 \geq 1n0​≥1
```

Solution

Here,

The growth of the f(n) function won't be exceed c * g(n) beyond n0n_0n0​ since the above conditions are met

Because c * g(n) grows faster than f(n), it can be any expression such as 5n, 10n, 2n22n^22n2, etc.

However, g(n) can't be 3n, 2n, or similar functions because they grow slower than 4n + 3.

Let's assume c * g(n) is 10n. In this scenario,

```text
c∗g(n)=10nc * g(n) = 10nc∗g(n)=10nf(n)=4n+3f(n) = 4n + 3f(n)=4n+3Since, f(n) cannot grow faster than c∗g(n)Since,\ f(n)\ cannot\ grow\ faster\ than\ c * g(n) Since, f(n) cannot grow faster than c∗g(n)4n+3≤10n [for all n≥1]4n+ 3 \leq  10n\ [for\ all\ n \geq 1]4n+3≤10n [for all n≥1]
```

![Big O Example](data:image/png;base64,)

As c∗g(n)≥f(n)c * g(n) \geq f(n)c∗g(n)≥f(n), we can say that:

```python
f(n) = O(g(n))
=> f(n) = O(n) [read as f(n) is big O of n]
```

Additionally, we could have chosen c * g(n) to be 2n22n^22n2 or 5n35n^35n3 as these functions also grow at a rate faster than 4n + 3.
